inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: This “15-point ceasefire plan” sent to Iran through Pakistan looks less like peace and more like a trap designed to manage the story: set terms Iran may reject, then pin the continued fighting on Iran. Its five counter-conditions put the real costs—ending aggression, compensation, and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz—on the table. Meanwhile, Israel’s skepticism and insistence on pre-emptive strikes expose how hollow the public peace talk may be. The powerful players seem to want negotiations on their terms while keeping escalation available, with blame assigned before the outcome is even known.
